SUBJECT MATTER Topic: Tongue Twisters for Clear Speaking References: Grade 1 Phonics Activities Materials: Big posters with 3 tongue twisters (with pictures): 1. “Peter Piper picked pickled peppers.” (Picture: Peter and peppers) 2. “Betty Botter bought butter.” (Picture: Betty and butter) 3. “Six snails slide slowly.” (Picture: snails sliding) Sound cards with pictures (e.g., popcorn for /p/, ball for /b/, snake for /s/). “Tongue Twister Stars/Badge” stickers. Thumbs-up chart for group activities. 76 III. PROCEDURE 1. Preparatory Activities A. Warm-Up (5 minutes): Play “Copy the Sound!”: Teacher says: “/p/ like popping popcorn!” (Students mimic popping and say /p/). Repeat with /b/ (bounce like a ball) and /s/ (slither like a snake). B. Motivation (3 minutes): Say: “Let’s play with silly sentences that twist our tongues! Who can say ‘Peter Piper’ fast without mixing up words?” 2. Developmental Activities Introduce Tongue Twisters: Show the poster and read “Peter Piper” slowly. Clap for each word. Point to the /p/ sound card every time you say “p.” Say it faster like a robot! Group Practice: Repeat with “Betty Botter” (/b/ sound) and “Six snails” (/s/ sound). Students take turns saying one line in pairs. 3. Analysis/Discussion Ask: “Why is ‘Peter Piper’ tricky to say?” (They’ll say: “Too many /p/ sounds!”). “How do tongue twisters help us?” (Answer: “They make our mouths strong for clear talking!”). 4. Guided Practice Tongue Twister Game: In small groups, students pick a tongue twister. 77 Say it slowly, then fast. Friends give a thumbs up if they hear the sounds clearly! Add fun: Hop or clap while saying it! IV. EVALUATION Use a simple checklist: Give “Tongue Twister Star” stickers to everyone who tries! Criteria (Great!) (Good!) (Keep Trying!) Says sounds clearly Tries slow and fast Participates with a smile V. AGREEMENT For homework: 1. Practice one tongue twister with your family. 2. Draw a picture of your favorite tongue twister (e.g., Peter Piper or snails). NOTE FOR TEACHER: Keep it playful! Praise effort over perfection. Use lots of movements (clapping, hopping) to make sounds memorable
